security_audit.summary: The static command findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code and TypeScript template literals, not shell execution. The API key findings are also false positives because the examples read provider keys from server-side environment variables rather than hardcoding or leaking secrets. I found semantic risks in unauthenticated AI route examples and missing prompt-injection guardrail guidance.

remediation.issue: Some AI route examples omit authentication.
remediation.suggestion: Update every route example to wrap handlers with withAuthRequired or clearly mark unauthenticated snippets as non-production examples.

remediation.issue: Prompt injection and data minimization guidance is missing.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance for validating user input, separating system instructions from user data, redacting secrets, and limiting tool permissions.

remediation.issue: Provider API key examples lack an explicit server-only warning.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short note that provider keys must stay server-side and must never be exposed to client components or logs.

semantic_findings.title: Public AI Route Examples Lack Authentication
semantic_findings.description: Several route examples read request bodies and call model APIs without wrapping the handler in authentication. Copying these examples directly can expose paid AI endpoints to unauthenticated use.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples show public POST handlers that call model APIs, while the skill separately says AI routes should verify session.user.id. This is a concrete copy-paste production risk, although the examples are documentation snippets.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Guardrails Are Not Shown
semantic_findings.description: Examples pass user-controlled messages, prompts, destinations, and agent topics into model calls without input boundaries or safety guidance. This can teach unsafe patterns for prompt-injection-prone workflows.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code is educational, but multiple snippets send untrusted request or event data directly into model prompts. I found no countervailing guidance on prompt injection, data minimization, or policy boundaries.

content.value_statement: Teams often lose time connecting chat, structured output, and agent workflows across Next.js services. This skill provides focused Vercel AI SDK patterns for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code users.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use the Vercel AI SDK for chat, structured output, generative UI, and agents.
Provides Next.js route handler examples for streamText, streamUI, and generateObject.
Shows OpenAI and Anthropic provider setup using server-side environment variables.
Demonstrates an Inngest background agent workflow with fixed loop control.
Includes client chat patterns using useChat and streaming data.
limitations: The examples are documentation snippets, not a complete application scaffold.
Some example routes need authentication before production use.
It does not cover image or video generation workflows.
It assumes Next.js App Router, React, Zod, and Inngest conventions.

use_cases.title: Add Streaming Chat
use_cases.description: Create a protected chat route and React client that stream model responses to users.

use_cases.title: Extract Structured Output
use_cases.description: Use Zod schemas and generateObject to convert user input into typed application data.

use_cases.title: Run Background Agents
use_cases.description: Move long-running research or planning tasks into Inngest workflows with bounded steps.

prompt_templates.title: Add Basic Chat
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new chat feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add an authenticated Vercel AI SDK streaming chat route and matching React client component to my Next.js app.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Structured Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a generateObject endpoint that validates the output with a Zod schema and returns typed application data.

prompt_templates.title: Create Generative UI
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced interface pattern with server-rendered components.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a streamUI route that returns React components from tool calls and keeps all tools server-side.

prompt_templates.title: Design Agent Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced background workflow with operational safeguards.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design an Inngest research agent with authentication, rate limits, bounded loops, schema validation, and persisted results.

output_examples.input: Create an authenticated streaming chat feature for a Next.js app.
output_examples.output: A short implementation plan covering provider setup, a protected POST route, a useChat client, and deployment checks.

output_examples.input: Build a structured itinerary generator from user input.
output: A suggested schema for itinerary fields.
Validation and error handling notes for production use.

output_examples.input: Move a multi-step research task into a background agent.
output_examples.output: A workflow outline with Inngest triggers, fixed step limits, model calls, result storage, and user notification points.

best_practices: Protect every AI API route with authentication and per-user rate limits.
Keep provider keys in server-only environment variables.
Use schemas and loop limits for structured output and agents.
anti_patterns: Do not copy unauthenticated examples into production routes.
Do not send secrets, raw logs, or private user data into prompts.
Do not run unbounded agent loops without timeout and step limits.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build Vercel AI SDK features such as streaming chat, structured output, generative UI, and background agents.

faq.question: Which coding assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it install dependencies automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents package names and code patterns that a developer can apply in a project.

faq.question: Is it production ready as written?
faq.answer: It is a starting point. Add authentication, rate limits, logging, monitoring, and privacy review before production use.

faq.question: Does it cover image or video generation?
faq.answer: No. The skill says to use ai-handler for Replicate or Fal.ai media generation workflows.

faq.question: Which frameworks does it assume?
faq.answer: It assumes Next.js App Router, React, the Vercel AI SDK, Zod, and optional Inngest workflows.
